title: ActiveCampaign Review (2026)
intro: Marketing automation platform with CRM/sales pipelines strongest on Plus and above, contact-based pricing. This review covers verified 2026 pricing, core CRM capabilities, limitations, and who should buy — based on official first-party sources.
summary: ActiveCampaign scores reflect first-party research — not hands-on product testing.
verdict: ActiveCampaign is best when marketing automation is the primary job and CRM pipelines on Plus+ are a bonus system of record—not when you only need a sales CRM. Contact-based pricing and no free plan shape value. Not hands-on tested.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Marketing automation UX is mature; CRM is approachable on Plus+ but the product is not pipeline-first like Pipedrive.
CRM pipelines exist and strengthen on Plus+; still secondary to marketing automation identity.
Automation is a category strength — especially when marketing + sales journeys connect.
Email marketing/automation is ActiveCampaign’s core advantage versus pure CRMs.
Campaign and CRM reporting are solid for SMB/mid-market automation buyers.
Automations, fields, and CRM customization are flexible for marketing-led teams.
Broad app ecosystem for marketing/sales stacks.
Contact-tier packaging and automation complexity create ongoing ops work.
Professional/Enterprise support growing contact volumes; very large enterprises may need suites.
No free plan; contact-based costs rise with list size — excellent if email automation is primary, weaker as CRM-only buy.

bestFor: Teams comparing HubSpot/Keap for email-first GTM
pricingSummary: No free plan. Contact-based USD annual at ~1k contacts: Starter $15, Plus $49, Professional $79, Enterprise $145 /mo. 14-day trial. CRM strongest Plus+.
limitations: Confirm live ActiveCampaign checkout; packaging can change.
whoShouldChoose: Choose ActiveCampaign when it matches your CRM buying criteria above.
whoShouldConsiderAlternatives: Consider alternatives like hubspot, keap, pipedrive if fit is weak.
